# Intent: Polished and Direct-Distribution-Ready Disk Steward

A macOS user can install and launch Disk Steward as a polished native menu-bar application, understand why it exists through a research-grounded 30-second product story, inspect its MIT-licensed public source, discover a truthful Homebrew distribution path, and receive a verifiably signed and notarized direct-distribution artifact without weakening the existing monitoring, evidence, privacy, or MCP behavior.

## Success Evidence

- `REQ-101` — A stable Xcode project builds and archives a real Disk Steward .app with permanent product identity, a visible menu-bar item, bundled resources, and the read-only MCP helper included in the product.
- `REQ-102` — The menu-bar dashboard presents capacity, growth, monitoring health, recency, and the evidence action in a compact Apple-like hierarchy that can be understood at a glance.
- `REQ-103` — The status board remains clear and operable in light and dark appearance and in active, paused, degraded, no-baseline, and error states, with meaningful accessibility labels and keyboard behavior.
- `REQ-104` — Existing whole-volume monitoring, watched-root evidence, export, read-only MCP, bounded retention, privacy exclusions, attribution honesty, and unprivileged fallback behavior continue to pass regression checks.
- `REQ-105` — The release workflow produces a Developer ID-signed, hardened-runtime, notarized, stapled direct-distribution artifact when the required Apple credential is available, and otherwise fails closed with an exact human action instead of claiming release readiness.
- `REQ-106` — Reproducible checks verify build, archive contents, nested-code signatures, entitlements, Gatekeeper assessment, launch behavior, tests, and absence of committed credentials or secrets.
- `REQ-107` — The user can turn local MCP agent access on or off from the app; off stops and removes the private IPC endpoint, refuses agent queries with honest guidance, persists across launches, and does not pause monitoring or delete evidence.
- `REQ-108` — Evidence follows a visible bounded lifecycle: recent exact detail becomes longer-lived summaries, snapshots are downsampled, anomalies have a finite detail window, database pressure produces explicit loss records, manual exports remain user-owned, and humans and agents can inspect the actual retained time ranges and storage usage.
- `REQ-109` — A persistent evidence chain distinguishes current presence from historical activity and correctly reconciles baseline, create, modify, truncate, rename, replace, delete, scope change, restart, partial scan, and path reuse; cleanup and task-impact queries never treat deleted, unknown, or out-of-scope objects as current consumers.
- `REQ-110` — The exact bundle created by the human-facing Export Current Evidence action gives a human or local agent enough bounded, integrity-verifiable current-state, growth, provenance, scope, coverage, lifecycle, and limitation evidence to select the next investigation without re-digging the application database.
- `REQ-111` — A user can add watched or excluded folders without depending on the crash-prone macOS open/save panel service, and a successful evidence export opens the completed evidence directory in Finder.
- `REQ-112` — A public MIT-licensed GitHub repository under KMerdan presents Disk Steward with an accurate modern README, real product screenshots, reproducible development instructions, explicit privacy and MCP boundaries, and honest release and Homebrew availability without publishing secrets or private runtime evidence.
- `REQ-113` — A polished, exactly 30-second promotional video uses real product visuals and a research-grounded transcript to explain the user problem, Disk Steward's evidence-first solution, and its non-destructive boundary without unsupported quantitative claims.
- `REQ-114` — A public Homebrew tap under KMerdan contains a maintainable Disk Steward cask manifest and activation instructions; before a notarized immutable release asset exists, the cask is explicitly disabled rather than distributing or implying trust in an unnotarized binary.

## Constraints

- Keep the product native Swift, AppKit, and SwiftUI on macOS 13 or newer, and preserve the existing Swift package as the reusable implementation boundary.
- Use Apple Developer Team G3P6TU385Y with proposed identifiers com.marudankiji.disksteward, com.marudankiji.disksteward.endpoint, and group.com.marudankiji.disksteward; validate availability before registration.
- Target direct distribution outside the Mac App Store with Developer ID, hardened runtime, secure timestamping, notarization, and stapling.
- The standard app must build, launch, monitor, export, and serve read-only MCP without the restricted Endpoint Security entitlement; keep the optional system extension as a separately gated product path.
- Do not store Apple credentials, private keys, account passwords, notarization profiles, or other secrets in the repository.
- The user owns the final Xcode Signing & Capabilities selection and Organizer archive, distribution, and notarization interaction; automation must remain credential-free and inspectable.
- Use system typography, semantic colors, materials, symbols, spacing, and native controls; avoid ornamental chrome that competes with storage health.
- Treat MCP availability as a local privacy boundary: fresh installs default agent access off, the setting is explicit and persistent, disabling it closes the Unix socket promptly, and monitoring plus human evidence export remain independent.
- Keep the evidence database bounded by both time and bytes; compaction may reduce precision but must never silently erase the fact that coverage was reduced.
- Never automatically delete a human-created evidence export; report app-owned export count and size and leave deletion to an explicit user action.
- Model paths as time-bounded bindings to file objects when stable filesystem identity is available; never equate path reuse with the same object without evidence.
- Absence proves deletion only within a complete observation of an unchanged scope; failed, partial, capped, excluded, or changed-scope observations must produce unknown or out-of-scope state and coverage evidence instead.
- Distinguish whole-volume capacity scope from file-detail monitored roots in every UI, export, and agent response; never use whole-volume capacity to imply whole-disk file coverage.
- A scan entry or time cap must bound one work slice rather than permanently pinning the same root to partial coverage; progress must be durable and complete reconciliation must occur only after a full root generation finishes.

## Non-Goals

- Submitting Disk Steward to the Mac App Store.
- Automatically creating, revoking, exporting, or installing Apple signing certificates or private keys.
- Making Endpoint Security approval or system-extension activation a prerequisite for the normal menu-bar app.
- Adding cleanup, deletion, cache-purging, or other destructive disk tools.
- Redesigning unrelated settings or evidence formats unless required for consistency with the new status board and bundle.
- Adding cloud accounts, telemetry, an externally reachable service, or credential storage.

## Assumptions

- `ASM-101` (medium) — The proposed bundle identifiers and App Group are available to Apple Developer Team G3P6TU385Y.
- `ASM-102` (medium) — The paid team can obtain or grant access to a Developer ID Application certificate for final direct distribution.
- `ASM-103` (high) — The existing Swift package implementation and 105 passing tests can be reused by an Xcode application target without changing evidence semantics.
